t344.description: Papers that solve two-, three- and four-body problems with contact interactions, including Efimov physics and scattering lengths.

t345.name: Formulations of quantum mechanics
t345.description: Papers that reformulate quantum mechanics and relate it to classical mechanics through trajectories, actions and hydrodynamics.

t346.name: Wigner function and phase-space methods
t346.description: Papers that develop Wigner functions and other phase-space representations for quantum dynamics.

t347.name: Relativistic wave equations
t347.description: Papers that study the Dirac and related relativistic equations, their interpretation, symmetries and field quantisation.

t348.name: Dunkl quantum mechanics
t348.description: Papers that solve oscillators and wave equations with Dunkl derivatives involving reflection operators.
t348.note: Narrow mathematical-physics niche; unstable across seeds.

t349.name: Generalised coherent states
t349.description: Papers that construct generalised coherent states and ladder operators for oscillators and other algebraic systems.

t350.name: Potential scattering theory
t350.description: Papers that develop transfer matrix and other methods for quantum and wave scattering from potentials.

t351.name: Bound states of model potentials
t351.description: Papers that solve Schrödinger, Klein-Gordon and Dirac equations for bound states of Coulomb-like and other model potentials.

t352.name: Exactly solvable potentials and oscillators
t352.description: Papers that find exact and approximate spectra of anharmonic oscillators and solvable potentials using supersymmetry, WKB and polynomials.

t353.name: Information thermodynamics and erasure
t353.description: Papers that bound the thermodynamic cost of erasure and information processing, including Maxwell demons and second-law formulations.

t354.name: Entropy production and fluctuation theorems
t354.description: Papers that define and measure entropy production, fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems.

t355.name: Quantum work statistics
t355.description: Papers that define and measure quantum work distributions, Jarzynski equalities and quasiprobability approaches to work.

t356.name: Work extraction and ergotropy
t356.description: Papers that bound extractable work and ergotropy and the roles of coherence and correlations as thermodynamic resources.

t357.name: Quantum Mpemba effect
t357.description: Papers that predict and observe faster relaxation or symmetry restoration from initial states further from equilibrium.

t358.name: Quantum speed limits
t358.description: Papers that derive and test quantum speed limits on state, operator and open-system evolution.

t359.name: Quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno effects
t359.description: Papers that analyse Zeno and anti-Zeno effects from frequent measurement and use Zeno dynamics for control.

t360.name: Quantum thermometry
t360.description: Papers that design probes and protocols for estimating temperature with quantum Fisher information, often at low temperatures.

t361.name: Critical quantum metrology
t361.description: Papers that use quantum phase transitions and criticality to enhance parameter estimation precision.

t362.name: Lieb-Robinson bounds
t362.description: Papers that prove Lieb-Robinson bounds, light cones and propagation speed limits for many-body and open quantum systems.

t363.name: Leggett-Garg inequalities
t363.description: Papers that test macrorealism through Leggett-Garg inequality violations in qubits, fields and continuous-variable systems.

t364.name: Decoherence and entanglement dynamics
t364.description: Papers that track how coherence, entanglement and quantum correlations evolve when small systems couple to noisy environments.
t364.note: Large catch-all genre of model calculations; broad but consistent in style.

t365.name: Gibbs sampling and thermal state preparation
t365.description: Papers that design quantum algorithms and Lindbladian dynamics to prepare thermal states and sample Gibbs distributions.

t366.name: Open quantum system master equations
t366.description: Papers that derive and solve Markovian and non-Markovian master equations and simulation methods for open quantum dynamics.
t366.note: Largest fine topic; a general methods pool that may hide sub-niches.

t367.name: Quantum tunnelling and tunnelling time
t367.description: Papers that model tunnelling through barriers and double wells and the time a particle spends tunnelling.

t368.name: Thermalisation and the ETH
t368.description: Papers that study how closed many-body systems thermalise, testing the eigenstate thermalisation hypothesis.

t369.name: Measurement-induced phase transitions
t369.description: Papers that study entanglement transitions in monitored circuits and continuously measured many-body systems.

t370.name: Quantum arrival times
t370.description: Papers that define and measure when a quantum particle arrives at a detector, including Bohmian and POVM approaches.

t371.name: Mathematical structure of quantum theory
t371.description: Papers that reconstruct or axiomatise quantum theory and examine Hilbert spaces, observables and operator algebras.

t372.name: History and ontology of quantum physics
t372.description: Papers that revisit the history of quantum theory and early debates about the reality of the wave function.
t372.note: Mixes historical studies with speculative ontology proposals; unstable across seeds.

t373.name: Bohmian mechanics
t373.description: Papers that develop, test and debate Bohmian trajectories, pilot-wave models and their relativistic extensions.

t374.name: Quantum reference frames
t374.description: Papers that develop quantum reference frames, relational frame changes and the Page-Wootters approach to time.

t375.name: Born rule derivations
t375.description: Papers that derive, justify or test the Born rule for quantum probabilities.

t376.name: Quantum causal inference
t376.description: Papers that model causal structures with quantum latent variables and test nonclassicality in causal networks.

t377.name: Indefinite causal order
t377.description: Papers that study process matrices, the quantum switch and indefinite causal order in quantum processes.

t378.name: Interpreting Bell's theorem
t378.description: Papers that argue over what Bell's theorem and Bell experiments imply about locality, realism and hidden variables.

t379.name: Quantum contextuality
t379.description: Papers that develop Kochen-Specker and generalised contextuality, noncontextuality inequalities and contextuality as a resource.

t380.name: Interpretations and the measurement problem
t380.description: Papers that propose and compare interpretations of quantum mechanics and philosophical accounts of measurement and reality.

t381.name: QBism and observer-centred views
t381.description: Papers that discuss QBism, agents, experience and consciousness in the interpretation of quantum theory.

t382.name: Holographic and Krylov complexity
t382.description: Papers that relate computational and Krylov complexity to black hole interiors and holographic duals.

t383.name: Generalised uncertainty principle
t383.description: Papers that build minimal-length quantum mechanics from generalised uncertainty principles motivated by quantum gravity.

t384.name: Spontaneous collapse models
t384.description: Papers that develop and constrain spontaneous wave-function collapse models such as CSL with experiments.

t385.name: Gravity tests with clocks and collapse
t385.description: Papers that test gravitational time dilation, the equivalence principle and gravity-related collapse with quantum systems.
t385.note: Joins gravity-related collapse tests with quantum clocks in gravity; unstable across seeds.

t386.name: Quantum clocks and time
t386.description: Papers that model quantum clocks, relational and emergent time, and quantum time dilation.

t387.name: Quantum cosmology and curved spacetime
t387.description: Papers that study quantum fields in curved spacetime, quantum cosmology and decoherence of inflationary perturbations.

t388.name: Entanglement near black holes
t388.description: Papers that compute how entanglement, steering and coherence degrade for observers near black holes and in non-inertial frames.

t389.name: Analogue Hawking radiation
t389.description: Papers that model and observe Hawking-like radiation in analogue horizons in fluids, condensates and optics.

t390.name: Black hole information problem
t390.description: Papers that study information loss, Page curves and the recovery of information from evaporating black holes.

t391.name: Gravitons and gravitational decoherence
t391.description: Papers that study graviton noise, quantum signatures of gravitational waves and gravity-induced decoherence.

t392.name: Gravitationally induced entanglement
t392.description: Papers that propose and analyse table-top tests of whether gravity can entangle masses and so must be quantum.

t393.name: Quantum correlations in neutrino oscillations
t393.description: Papers that apply coherence, entanglement and other quantum-information measures to neutrino flavour oscillations and their decoherence.

t394.name: Simulating collective neutrino oscillations
t394.description: Papers that model and quantum-simulate many-body collective neutrino flavour oscillations in dense astrophysical environments.
t394.note: Unstable across seeds; splits from t393 differently by seed.

t395.name: Entanglement at colliders
t395.description: Papers that measure entanglement, Bell violation and quantum tomography in top-quark, Higgs and other collider events.

t396.name: Entanglement in scattering processes
t396.description: Papers that study entanglement generated in particle scattering, from Compton scattering to partons and nucleon interactions.

t397.name: Entanglement harvesting
t397.description: Papers that compute how Unruh-DeWitt detectors extract entanglement from quantum field vacua under different motions and spacetimes.

t398.name: Unruh effect and accelerated detectors
t398.description: Papers that study the Unruh effect and how acceleration affects correlations and coherence of Unruh-DeWitt detectors.
